newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Banco Commercial Portugues to boost stake in BPA.
newsitem.headline: Banco Commercial Portugues to boost stake in BPA.

text.p: Portugal's biggest private bank, Banco Comercial Portugues, said on Friday it planned to buy 25 percent of Banco Portugues do Atlantico from insurer Companhia de Seguros Imperio, boosting its controlling stake.
The purchase raises BCP's stake in BPA to 75.1 percent from 50.1 percent. BCP bought BPA, then Portugal's second biggest bank, for 308 billion escudos ($1.8 billion) in March 1995.
Imperio, part of the Mello group, presently holds a stake of about 46 percent in BPA.

"Banco Comercial Portugues today announced its intention to acquire 27.5 million shares of Banco Portugues do Atlantico, representing 25 percent of its share capital, from Companhia de Seguros Imperio," BCP said in a statement.
The price is 2,800 escudos per share, the same amount offered in the public tender offer in March 1995.
"As contractually established, BCP has the right to place or purchase the shares held by Imperio, which may be exercised until March 2000," it added.

BCP said it would finance the operation from its own resources and through the issue of subordinated perpetual bonds, eligible as "Upper Tier Two", therefore avoiding the need for any share capital increase.

"The restructuring and integration of subsidiaries into specialised holding companies, and the measures undertaken to bring down staff numbers, underpinned the strategic importance of raising BCP's shareholding to a level more proportionate to the degree of influence and control that we exercise upon BPA," said BCP chairman and CEO Jorge Jardim Goncalves.

"The increase of BCP's shareholding from 50.1 percent to 75.1 percent of Atlantico's capital reflects our...confidence in the outcome of the revamping of (Atlantico's) commercial activity and rationalisation," he added.
The acquisition of the stake is subject to acceptance by the Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) of BCP's request for an exemption from a public tender offer, BCP said.

BCP hit a high of 3,348 escudos on Lisbon bourse after the announcement and later eased back to 3,300, up 56, in volume of 60,700 shares in mid-morning. Imperio rose 26 escudos to 1,029 in volume of 6,200. ($1=174.562 escudos)
